meta.title: Our Class Timetable
meta.textType: functional: a class timetable with notes

paragraphs: My name is Lily, and this is our class timetable. It's a new term, and Teacher Kim gives us a copy. School starts at half past eight a.m. It ends at half past three p.m. Lunch is at twelve o'clock, and we can play until one o'clock. Teacher Kim points at the big timetable on the wall. Every subject has a day and a time on it. "Please copy the days and the times," she says. Mia and Leo sit next to me and look at it. "Which lesson is the second one on Monday?" asks Leo. "It's science," says Mia.

On Monday, language is at half past eight. Science is at twenty past nine. Geography is on Monday afternoon, at one o'clock. On Tuesday, we have gym at ten past ten. Gym is twice a week, on Tuesday and Thursday. Each gym lesson is forty-five minutes long. On Tuesday afternoon, the class goes to the library at one o'clock. Art is on Wednesday afternoon, at ten to two. On Thursday, gym is at ten past ten again. On Friday, the class meeting is at two o'clock. "What do we do at a class meeting?" I ask. "We talk about the week," says Teacher Kim.

Under the table, I write some notes. "You should bring a sports shirt on Tuesday and Thursday." "You should bring your library book on Tuesday." "We should be in the classroom at twenty past eight." Leo reads my notes and smiles. "Should I bring my sports shirt on Wednesday, too?" he asks. Mia says, "No, there is no gym on Wednesday." We are going to have a good term.

On Monday evening, I put my sports shirt in my school bag. Gym is tomorrow. I do this at the door at home. Pip comes and sniffs the bag. "Pip, the shirt is for gym, not for you," I say. Now look at my timetable. When do we have art? How long is gym?
text.summary: Lily copies the class timetable for the new term into her notebook. She writes notes with advice, and she asks two questions about art and gym.
